title: Fusion ladder, calibration and kill gate 5
description: The measured result of the fusion ladder, including kill gate 5's verdict. Ratified 2026-08-17 in B2-B6. This contract exists because the receipt is the artifact a judge reads to decide whether the physics claim is real, and every way that claim could be overstated was available while it was being written. Four shapes are therefore invalid by construction rather than by review. A comparison cannot report a margin without the interval, the observation count and the episode count that produced it, because a margin alone is a number with no support. A comparison's direction is a four-valued enum rather than a boolean, because a two-valued verdict reports an interval lying entirely below zero as an absence of difference, which hides a measured harm behind a null; the operator's own first version of this code did exactly that. A gate verdict must carry a statement, so a bare 'PASSED' cannot travel without the sentence that qualifies it. And an infeasible risk ceiling must carry a reason, so 'no threshold was found' cannot be mistaken for 'no threshold was needed'. The ablation block must carry both the nominal and the multiplicity-corrected rule with the deciding rule named, because reporting only the rule that was applied would conceal that they disagree. Revised 2026-08-19 in D7 (SPACE-S6, SPACE-S7): the fields the clustered bootstrap and the cross-split correction added are declared rather than tolerated by open objects, a corrected interval must now carry the resolution of the endpoint it is read at, and the ablation must state whether the arm the product ships is the arm it recommends. That last one is required because the two stopped agreeing: the corridor block's win does not survive correction over the family the rule reads, while the queue is still ranked by it, and a single shipped_arm field could report only one of those. The version stays at 0.1.0 on the same reasoning as the D3 tightening below: the writer in this repository emits every newly required field, so no document has to be rewritten. Revised 2026-08-19 in D3 (ENG-S1): the root is closed and the document version is pinned with a const. Before this, a receipt written by an older script validated against the current schema and was read as current, and a root key nothing declares could be added without any reader noticing. The receipt already carried schema_version 0.1.0 and the contract path, so no document had to be rewritten and the version stays at 0.1.0: this tightening rejects only shapes no writer in this repository produces.

contract.description: Path to this contract, written by the generator so a reader of the receipt alone can find the schema it was validated against. Declared here because the root is closed.

schema_version.description: Pinned so a receipt written by an older script cannot validate against this schema and be read as current. Bumping the contract version above means bumping this const.

split_manifest_sha256.description: Digest of the split manifest these results were measured against. Without it a receipt cannot be tied to the splits that produced it, and a re-split would silently invalidate every number here.

feature_admissibility.description: Which source fields each block read, checked against FIELD_CLASSIFICATION. A block that read a post-observation field is a leak, so the check is recorded rather than assumed.

arm_ladder.description: The ladder as declared, so a reader can see which arms existed before any were compared.

size_matched_control.description: Separates the cost of a smaller training partition from the cost of unseen entities. Required reading before any cold-split drop is attributed to entity novelty.

ci95.description: Null only when the comparison is unmeasurable, which the direction must then say.

direction.description: Four states, not two. 'reference_better' is a measured harm and a stronger finding than 'indistinguishable'; collapsing the two reports harm as an absent effect. 'unmeasurable' is distinct again: it means the resampling could not produce an interval, which is a fact about the method rather than about the models.

n_groups.description: Episodes resampled. Required because an interval over observations rather than episodes is too narrow by roughly the mean group size, and the only way a reader can tell which was done is to see both counts.

governing_interval.description: Which grouping produced the published bound, or the union of both. Declared so a reader does not have to infer from three intervals which one the verdict was read from.

in_multiplicity_family.description: False for a reported interval that the correction does not count. Declared and paired with a reason, because an interval published beside a corrected family and not in it is the shape that lets an eighth comparison be reported against a family of seven.

challenger_auc.description: The challenger's own AUC, carried beside the difference so the interval and the pair of point estimates it was taken between cannot drift apart. Written only by the auc_comparisons block.

reference_auc.description: The reference arm's AUC, the partner of challenger_auc.

then.description: An unmeasurable comparison has to say why, or it is indistinguishable from a tie in every downstream reading.
A comparison published outside the corrected family has to say why. Without the reason, an interval reported beside a family of seven and not counted in it is indistinguishable from a miscount.

percentile_resolution.description: Whether the bootstrap had enough draws to resolve the quantile the corrected interval is read at. A Bonferroni correction over a 21-comparison family puts the endpoint at alpha/42 in each tail, and a percentile bootstrap can only report a quantile it has draws for. The failure is silent without this: the interval comes back looking like any other interval.

clustering_diagnostics.description: What each grouping actually grouped. Both are required because a grouped bootstrap whose groups are all of size 1 is an ungrouped bootstrap reporting the same interval under a name that implies otherwise, and the only way a reader can tell is to see both group counts. Gate 5's episode grouping is exactly that case on this corpus: 88 groups over 88 observations.

then.description: An unmeasurable intraclass correlation must say why. A null ICC with no reason reads as no clustering, which is the opposite of what one group per observation means.

verdict.description: NOT_ESTABLISHED and FAILED are separate outcomes. A point estimate in the right direction with an interval spanning zero has not established the claim; a point estimate in the wrong direction with an interval clearing zero has failed it. Folding them together would let either be reported as the other.

statement.description: The verdict in prose, carrying the numbers it rests on. A bare enum can be quoted out of context; a statement cannot.

gate_text.description: The gate as originally worded, so a reader can check the verdict against the claim rather than against a paraphrase of it.

per_split.description: The gate is worded against one split and taken there, but every split is reported beside it, because a gain that appears only where entities are shared is a different claim from one that survives a cold split.

additionalProperties.description: The evidence lists are required even when empty, because 'retained on nothing' and 'retained on two splits' are different claims and a bare decision cannot tell them apart.

shipped_arm_was_measured.description: False when the rule selects a block combination no arm on the ladder fitted. Its score would then come from a fresh fit that no interval in this receipt covers, and the receipt has to admit that rather than quote a number for it.

rules_disagree_on.description: Required even when empty. Reporting only the rule that was applied would conceal that another defensible rule reaches a different answer.

min_train_justification.description: Why the floor is where it is. A threshold that excludes a split from the decision needs a measured reason, or it is indistinguishable from excluding the split that gave an inconvenient answer.

shipped_blocks.description: The blocks the product ships, which is what the ranker is built from. Not the blocks the rule recommends: see recommended_blocks, and shipped_arm_vs_recommendation for the difference.

shipped_arm_vs_recommendation.description: Required, and required to carry a statement, because the two can differ and after the D7 correction they do. Reporting one field called shipped_arm would either put the recommendation's name on the queue's numbers or hide that a block the queue ranks by has lost its interval to the multiplicity correction.

fragility.description: Every way a RETAIN could be thinner than it looks, collected rather than left for a reader to reconstruct from four nested blocks. A concern list that could be empty would make a qualified verdict indistinguishable from an unqualified one, so a row exists only when it has something to say.

caveat.description: The retain decision reads test-set comparisons, so the shipped arm's score is optimistic. Required so the number cannot travel without the sentence.

then.description: An infeasible ceiling must say why. Without a reason, 'no threshold' reads as 'no threshold needed'.

achieved_on_test.description: The risk the calibration-chosen threshold actually reached on test. Required whenever the ceiling was feasible, because a ceiling chosen on calibration and never verified is a promise, not a measurement.

held.description: Null when nothing was kept, which is not the same as the ceiling failing.

split_result._closed_because: Renaming an optional block used to validate. Five measured sections (selective, ood, multiplicity_adjusted, ensemble, test_positive_rate) could be renamed here and the receipt still passed, after which the console published null for every one of them and the risk and coverage section vanished from the page with no note. A closed object turns that rename into a validation failure at the writer.

test_positive_rate.description: Fraction of the test partition in the signal-present class. Emitted by run_fusion.py and previously undeclared, which the open object allowed.

train_positive_rate.description: Fraction of the training partition in the signal-present class. Emitted beside test_positive_rate so a reader can see whether the class balance shifts between partitions, and previously undeclared.

auc_comparisons.description: The same comparison shape applied to area under the ROC curve. Declared because the root of this block is closed and because the AUC row was the one published gain in this receipt with no interval on it: two arms' AUCs sat side by side in `arms` and nothing measured the difference. Keyed by challenger, and each entry carries in_multiplicity_family false with its reason, because AUC decides no gate and the family size was fixed by the ladder before anything was fitted.

governing_interval.description: Which grouping produced the published bound. Both are measured and the union is published, so a reader can see whether the verdict rests on the grouping that happened to be wider.

direction_adjusted.description: Required, and three-valued for the same reason 'direction' is four-valued. A correction that can only express a surviving gain makes a surviving harm unrepresentable, and a rule reading it then treats a missing correction as an absent harm.

aurc_shipped_arm_name.description: The arm the aurc_shipped_* figures describe, written down rather than left to a reader who would have to know a constant in a script to find out.

aurc_shipped_not_measured_reason.description: Present instead of the comparison when the shipped arm is the reference or the challenger. A self-comparison has a margin of exactly zero by construction, which reads as an absence of benefit rather than an absence of a comparison.

risk_ratio_state.description: Why the ratio is or is not a number. A null ratio from an empty cell and a null ratio from a zero denominator are different facts, and both differ from 'not computed'. On a cold split every test row is novel by construction, so the unflagged cell is empty and the axis carries no contrast at all; without this field that reads as a failed measurement.

then.description: A split that is not degraded must carry results. A receipt with neither a result nor a stated reason is the shape that lets a silent failure pass as a completed run.
A degraded split says what it could not do.
